title: Genuina principia doctrinae de statu aequilibrii et motu corporum tam perfecte flesibilium quam elasticorum

deep.reconstruction:
Context (§§XXIII–XXV of E410, Problem I): a uniform, perfectly flexible heavy string, the catenary. On the previous page Euler set x as the vertical abscissa, measured upward, and y as the horizontal ordinate. From the equilibrium equations dT = β dx and T dφ = β dy he found T = βx + C, then the first integral dy = D dx/√((βx+C)² − D²), the logarithmic integral for y, and βs = √((βx+C)² − D²) + E.

This page:
(1) The tension T = βx + C grows linearly with height. This is the classical fact that the tension at a point equals the weight of a string segment whose length is that point's height above a fixed 'directrix' level.
(2) Fixing constants. Take the origin at the point A where the curve meets the axis, so that x = y = s = 0 there. Then βy/D = ln[(βx + C + √((βx+C)² − D²))/(C + √(C² − D²))] and βs = √((βx+C)² − D²) − √(C² − D²).
(3) Further choose A as the vertex, where the tangent is horizontal, so dy/dx = ∞ at x = 0. This forces D = C. Setting C = βa gives dy = a dx/√(2ax + x²). Hence y = a ln[(x + a + √(2ax + x²))/a] and s = √(2ax + x²), so dy : dx = a : s. In modern form this is x + a = a cosh(y/a) and s = a sinh(y/a). The tension is βa at the lowest point and β(x + a) at M.
(4) §XXV, inverse problem. A chain hangs between two points M, N at equal height. Given the sag AX = x and the half-length AM = s, the relation s² = 2ax + x² gives the parameter a = (s² − x²)/(2x). The next page then derives the half-span y = a ln((s+x)/(s−x)), the end slopes, the end tensions β(s² + x²)/(2x), and a small-sag expansion.

The purpose of the passage is to illustrate Euler's 'genuine principles' (the local balance equations for tension and curvature) on the classical catenary before he moves on to the velaria (sail curve).
errors: No mathematical errors on this page; all formulas check. With x = 0 the general formulas give y = s = 0. Putting D = C gives (βx+C)² − C² = β²(2ax + x²). The relation (x + a + s)/a = (s+x)/(s−x) confirms the next page.
Minor typo on the NEXT page only: the series is written for L((x+s)/(x−s)) where L((s+x)/(s−x)) is meant.

ideas.what: Catenary equation via tension balance; y = a ln((x+a+√(2ax+x²))/a), s = √(2ax+x²)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jacob and Johann Bernoulli, Leibniz, Huygens (1691)
ideas.where_published: Methodus inveniendi (E65, 1744), Mechanica, and other Euler texts

ideas.what: Tension proportional to height above a fixed level (T = β(x + a)), with minimum βa at the vertex
ideas.where_published: standard in Euler's mechanics writings; also Truesdell's 'Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies'

ideas.what: Determining the catenary parameter from sag and half-length: a = (s² − x²)/(2x)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a textbook rederivation of the catenary, its tension, and its sag–length relation. These were known since 1691 and are discussed by Truesdell in his commentary on E410. Nothing new.
transcription_corrections: The transcription matches the image well. The trailing 'XM' is the catchword leading into the next page ('XM = XN = y = ...'). 'Tab. VIII. Fig. 6.' is the marginal figure reference beside §XXV.
